verified.bloom_gates: G2 partial — a concrete, calendar-dated regulatory commitment (accepted NDA, Priority Review, fixed PDUFA date). No G1 named counterparty and no G3 specific currently-unpriced figure; LGMD2I/R9 is ultra-rare with a small addressable market.
verified.edge: L — Phase 3 FORTIFY already met all primary/secondary endpoints, so the Nov-27 approval is high-probability and largely de-risked/priced; ultra-rare indication is a small value driver for a ~$20B+ company whose thesis is the acoramidis (Attruby) ATTR-CM commercial ramp. The two other "imminent" Ph3 readouts cited in triage (encaleret ADH1, infigratinib achondroplasia) have already read out positive (Oct 2025 and Feb 2026) and are fired.
verified.primary_source: BridgeBio press release / GlobeNewswire, "FDA Acceptance and Priority Review of NDA for BBP-418" (May 27, 2026; PDUFA Nov 27, 2026); infigratinib PROPEL 3 topline (Feb 12, 2026); encaleret ADH1 Phase 3 topline (Oct 29, 2025)
verified.analysis: BBIO has one genuine dated, forward binary remaining: the BBP-418 PDUFA on Nov 27, 2026, which would be the first approved therapy for any limb-girdle muscular dystrophy. However, positive Phase 3 data already de-risks the approval, the LGMD2I/R9 market is ultra-rare, and BBIO's valuation is dominated by the acoramidis commercial story rather than this asset — so edge is low and the catalyst is largely priced. The triage's other cited catalysts (encaleret, infigratinib) are stale: both Phase 3 readouts already fired positive months ago, leaving only planned NDA submissions/launches ahead, not readouts.
